1. A single field repeating is fine; the PK can be SCLN+SROW, which is unique.
2. Entity integrity holds; only domain and referential are violated.
ex.az: 单个字段重复不等于违反；SCLN+SROW 可作 PK。

demo.query:
SELECT 'duplicate SID' AS PROBLEM, SID FROM STUDENT GROUP BY SID HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
UNION ALL
SELECT 'referential: CID ' || CID, SID FROM STUDENT WHERE CID IS NOT NULL AND CID NOT IN (SELECT CID FROM CLUB)
UNION ALL
SELECT 'domain: CNO ' || CNO, SID FROM STUDENT WHERE CNO NOT BETWEEN 1 AND 30;
demo.note: One query, three checks.

cards.t: Maintaining referential integrity when a parent record is removed
cards.tz: 删除 parent 记录时保持参照完整性
cards.en:
Intuition: before a shop closes, you clear its shelves. Products can't stay listed under a shop that's gone.

The rule: before (or together with) removing a parent record, either

  • delete the related child records (Checkpoint 4.3(d): the records of all products sold at that shop are removed as well); or
  • update their foreign key to another valid value or NULL (Exercise Q2(c): players of a withdrawn team).

Automatic: FOREIGN KEY (SID) REFERENCES SHOP(SID) ON DELETE CASCADE (or ON DELETE SET NULL).

Warning (Exercise Q3(f)): cascaded deletes lose data permanently; to get it back, roll back / restore from a backup.

Exam wording: "Delete (or update) the related records in the host table first, then delete the record in the parent table."
cards.zh:
直觉：店铺关门前要先清货架，产品不能挂在已不存在的店下。

规则：删除 parent 记录之前（或同时）：删除相关 child 记录（Checkpoint 4.3(d)：该店所有产品一并删除），或把它们的 FK 改成其他有效值或 NULL。

自动：ON DELETE CASCADE（或 ON DELETE SET NULL）。注意：级联删除会永久失去数据，要靠 rollback / 还原备份取回。

考试写法："Delete (or update) the related records in the host table first, then delete the record in the parent table."

ex.q: Shop S2 closes. Write the SQL in the correct order.
ex.a:
DELETE FROM PRODUCT WHERE SID = 'S2';
DELETE FROM SHOP WHERE SID = 'S2';
Children first, then parent (demo).
ex.az: 先删 child，再删 parent。

ex.q: Use ON DELETE SET NULL so products of a closed shop stay but are marked 'no shop'.
ex.a: Declare SID CHAR(2) REFERENCES SHOP(SID) ON DELETE SET NULL; then DELETE FROM SHOP WHERE SID='S2' sets Ruler and Eraser's SID to NULL (code block).
ex.az: ON DELETE SET NULL 自动把 FK 设为 NULL。

ex.q: A student runs DELETE FROM SHOP WHERE SID='S2'; first. What happens with FKs on?
ex.a:
1. Rejected: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed (S2 is still referenced).
2. Delete the products first.
ex.az: 次序错：被拒。

demo.note: Correct order: both deletes succeed, no broken references.

notes.t: Host table: if a shop is deleted, its products' SID becomes NULL.
notes.tz: host 表：店被删时 SID 自动变 NULL。

notes.t: Delete S2: allowed because of SET NULL.
notes.tz: 删除 S2：因 SET NULL 而允许。

notes.t: Ruler and Eraser now have SID NULL.
notes.tz: Ruler、Eraser 的 SID 变 NULL。

code.out:
PID  PNAME   SID 
---  ------  ----
1    Pen     S1  
2    Ruler   NULL
3    Eraser  NULL

cards.en:
Intuition: the "undo" button, or loading a saved game after you lose.

The rule: a rollback means restoring a database to its previous state. Errors (wrong SQL, wrong order, a program aborted halfway, hardware failure) may corrupt the integrity of data. So we make a backup regularly, and when needed we roll back the database using the backup.

  • Changes made after the backup are lost by the restore, so back up often.
  • In SQL, a transaction can be undone before COMMIT: BEGIN; ... ROLLBACK;

Exam wording: "Roll back the database to its previous state using the backup, to restore data integrity."
cards.zh:
直觉：就是"复原"按钮，或输了游戏后读取存档。

规则：rollback 是把数据库还原到之前的状态。错误（SQL 写错、次序错、程序中途中止、硬件故障）可能破坏数据完整性，所以要定期备份，需要时用备份回滚。备份之后的改动会丢失，所以要常备份。SQL 中 transaction 可用 BEGIN; … ROLLBACK; 撤销。

考试写法："Roll back the database to its previous state using the backup, to restore data integrity."

ex.q: BEGIN; DELETE FROM STUDENT; ROLLBACK; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM STUDENT; (5 rows before). Output?
ex.a:
1. ROLLBACK undoes everything since BEGIN.
2. Output 5 (see code).
ex.az: ROLLBACK 撤销删除 → 5。

ex.q: A backup was made Monday. Wrong SQL ran Wednesday. Restore on Wednesday. What about Tuesday's new records?
ex.a:
1. They were not in Monday's backup → lost.
2. They must be re-entered. That is why backups should be regular.
ex.az: 星期二的新记录会丢，要重新输入。

ex.q: "Rollback means deleting the wrong records by hand." Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Fixing by hand may miss rows and can't recover deleted data.
2. Rollback = restoring the whole database to a previous state from a backup.
ex.az: rollback 是还原到之前状态，不是手动删。

frames.en: Each night, copy the whole database to a backup file.
frames.zh: 每晚把数据库复制到备份文件。

frames.en: Wrong SQL, wrong order or an aborted program corrupts the data.
frames.zh: 错误 SQL 或程序中止破坏数据。

frames.en: Restore the backup: the database returns to its previous state.
frames.zh: 还原备份：回到之前状态。

frames.en: Re-run the correct statements; re-enter changes made after the backup.
frames.zh: 重新执行正确语句，补回备份后的改动。

notes.t: Start a transaction: changes are not final yet.
Inside the transaction the table looks empty.

notes.tz: 撤销 BEGIN 之后的所有改动。

cards.t: Example: SQL statements run in the wrong order
cards.en:
Intuition: "empty the box, then put new things in" is very different from "put new things in, then empty the box".

The case: new school year. Plan: (1) delete 6A students, (2) promote 5A to 6A.

DELETE FROM STUDENT WHERE CLASS = '6A';
UPDATE STUDENT SET CLASS = '6A' WHERE CLASS = '5A';

Run in the wrong order: UPDATE first makes everyone 6A; then DELETE removes every 6A student → the table is empty.

Fix: roll back (restore the backup), then run in the correct order.

Exam wording: "The order of SQL statements matters. Restore the database from the backup and run the statements in the correct order."
cards.zh:
直觉："先清空箱子再放新东西"和"先放新东西再清空"结果完全不同。

情况：新学年：(1) 删除 6A，(2) 把 5A 升到 6A。若次序弄错：先 UPDATE 让所有人变 6A，再 DELETE 就把全部删掉，表变空。

补救：rollback（还原备份）后按正确次序执行。

考试写法："The order of SQL statements matters. Restore the database from the backup and run the statements in the correct order."

ex.q: 3 students in 6A and 7 in 5A. Rows left after (a) correct order, (b) wrong order?
ex.a:
(a) DELETE 3, UPDATE 7 → 7 rows, all 6A.
(b) UPDATE → 10 rows 6A, DELETE → 0 rows.

ex.q: Show the correct order on the sample table.
ex.a: Demo: after both statements, Kit and Lam remain in 6A.
ex.az: 演示：Kit、Lam 在 6A。

ex.q: After the wrong order, a teacher tries to fix it by re-inserting the 5A students from memory. Problem?
ex.a:
1. Data from memory may be incomplete or wrong (other fields are lost).
2. Correct: roll back from the backup, then rerun in order.
ex.az: 凭记忆补回不可靠，应还原备份。

demo.setup:
CREATE TABLE STUDENT (SID CHAR(5) PRIMARY KEY, NAME VARCHAR(40), CLASS CHAR(2));
INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('03001','Hans','6A'),('03002','Ivy','6A'),('03003','Jean','6A'),('03101','Kit','5A'),('03102','Lam','5A');
demo.note: Correct order. Swap the two lines and run again: the result is empty.

cards.t: Lab 4.1: backup with mysqldump and restore with mysql
cards.en:
Intuition: mysqldump writes your whole database down as a "recipe" of SQL statements; mysql cooks it again.

Backup (Command Prompt): mysqldump -u root -p SCHOOL > school.sql

Restore (rollback): mysql -u root -p -h localhost SCHOOL < school.sql

The file holds statements like CREATE TABLE and INSERT INTO that rebuild every table with the data at backup time. If 'mysqldump' is not recognised, add the MySQL bin folder to the PATH environment variable.

SQLite equivalent: sqlite3 school.db .dump > school.sql and sqlite3 new.db < school.sql.

Exam wording: "Export the database to an SQL file regularly with mysqldump; restore it with mysql."
cards.zh:
直觉：mysqldump 把整个数据库写成一份 SQL"食谱"，mysql 再照着重新做出来。

备份：mysqldump -u root -p SCHOOL > school.sql
还原：mysql -u root -p -h localhost SCHOOL < school.sql

文件里是 CREATE TABLE 和 INSERT INTO 语句。若找不到 mysqldump，要把 MySQL 的 bin 文件夹加进 PATH。SQLite 对应：.dump。

考试写法："Export the database to an SQL file regularly with mysqldump; restore it with mysql."

ex.q: User admin backs up SHOP to shop_bak.sql, later restores on localhost. Commands?
ex.a:
mysqldump -u admin -p SHOP > shop_bak.sql
mysql -u admin -p -h localhost SHOP < shop_bak.sql
ex.az: 两条命令如上。

ex.q: What is inside a dump file?
ex.a: Plain SQL: CREATE TABLE for each table and INSERT INTO for each row (see the SQLite .dump output in the code block).
ex.az: CREATE TABLE 和 INSERT 语句。

ex.q: A student writes mysqldump -u root -p SCHOOL < school.sql to back up. What's wrong?
ex.a:
1. < reads from a file; a backup must write to it with >.
2. Remember: dump > out, mysql < in.
ex.az: 箭头方向错：备份用 >，还原用 <。

code.src:
mysqldump -u root -p SCHOOL > school.sql
mysql -u root -p -h localhost SCHOOL < school.sql

notes.t: Export database SCHOOL as user root (ask password) into school.sql.
notes.tz: 把 SCHOOL 导出到 school.sql。

notes.t: Run school.sql on host localhost to rebuild SCHOOL (rollback).
notes.tz: 在 localhost 执行 school.sql 还原 SCHOOL。

code.out: (backup file created; after restore the tables match the backup)

notes.t: A small table to back up.
SQLite's dump command: prints the SQL that rebuilds the database.
notes.tz: SQLite 的 dump：输出重建数据库的 SQL。

cards.t: Rolling back an interrupted batch of updates
cards.tz: 中途中断的更新要回滚
cards.en:
Intuition: paying a friend has two halves: money leaves you, money reaches them. If only the first half happens, money vanishes.

Checkpoint 4.4: PAYMENT(TID, PAYERID, PAYEEID, AMOUNT, TTIME), ACCOUNT(AID, UNAME, DEPOSIT). Each payment: payer's deposit − amount; payee's deposit + amount.

A program for 10,000 payments was aborted by an error; nobody knows where.

  • What to do: roll back the database to its previous state (backup before the program), then run it again.
  • Why: some payments may be halfway through (payer subtracted, payee not added), so data integrity is corrupted; rerunning directly would apply some payments twice.

In SQL, put both updates of one payment in one transaction.
cards.zh:
直觉：付款有两半：钱从你那里出去、钱到对方那里。只做了前一半，钱就凭空消失。

Checkpoint 4.4：处理 10,000 笔付款的程序中途出错中止，不知停在哪里。

  • 做法：把数据库回滚到之前状态（程序执行前的备份），再重新执行。
  • 原因：有些付款可能只做了一半，数据完整性被破坏；直接重跑会令部分付款做两次。

SQL 中应把同一笔付款的两个 UPDATE 放在同一个 transaction。

ex.q: Account A1 pays A2 $50 (TID 77). Write SQL so both updates happen together or not at all.
ex.a:
BEGIN;
UPDATE ACCOUNT SET DEPOSIT = DEPOSIT - 50 WHERE AID = 'A1';
UPDATE ACCOUNT SET DEPOSIT = DEPOSIT + 50 WHERE AID = 'A2';
COMMIT;
On error before COMMIT → ROLLBACK.
ex.az: 两个 UPDATE 放在同一 transaction。

ex.q: A1 has $100 and tries to pay $150. The first UPDATE breaks CHECK (DEPOSIT >= 0). What should happen?
ex.a:
1. The first update fails.
2. ROLLBACK so the second (+150 to A2) is not kept either. See code: deposits stay 100 and 20.
ex.az: 失败后 ROLLBACK，两边都不变。

ex.q: After the crash, a clerk just reruns the program from the start. Why is this wrong?
ex.a:
1. Payments finished before the crash would be applied twice.
2. Half-done payments stay wrong.
3. Must roll back first, then rerun.
ex.az: 直接重跑会重复扣款，应先回滚。

frames.en: Start the payment. Nothing is final yet.
If the program stops now, A1 lost $50 but A2 got nothing: integrity broken. ROLLBACK puts A1 back to 100.
frames.zh: 此时中止：A1 少了钱但 A2 没收到；ROLLBACK 还原。

frames.en: A2: 20 → 70, then COMMIT makes both changes final together.

notes.t: Start one payment as a transaction.
notes.tz: 把一笔付款作为 transaction 开始。

notes.t: Take $150 from A1: fails the CHECK (only $100).
notes.tz: 从 A1 扣 150：违反 CHECK。

notes.t: Give $150 to A2: this half would succeed.
notes.tz: 给 A2 加 150：这半会成功。

notes.t: An error happened, so undo the whole payment.

code.out:
Error: CHECK constraint failed: DEPOSIT >= 0 (19)
AID  UNAME    DEPOSIT
---  -------  -------
A1   Tom Ho   100    
A2   May Lee  20

cards.t: Chapter Exercise: linking table STARRING and table design
cards.tz: 章末练习：连接表 STARRING 与表设计
cards.en:
Intuition: one actor is in many films, and one film has many actors. A single "FID" box on the actor's card can hold only one film, so we keep a separate list of actor–film pairs.

Exercise Q3: ACTOR(AID, ANAME, SEX, AGE, FID), FILM(FID, FNAME, FYEAR).

  1. (a) Actors star in films.
  2. (b) SEX as Boolean → domain {TRUE, FALSE}.
  3. (c) ACTOR: PK AID, FK FID; FILM: PK FID, FK N/A.
  4. (d) Why STARRING(FID, AID, CTYPE, ROLE)? With one FID field, an actor can only be linked to one film. STARRING stores one row per actor–film pair, PK FID+AID.

Exercise Q1: MEALORDER with no unique field violates entity integrity; form controls that only allow numbers = validation, which keeps domain integrity.
cards.zh:
直觉：一个演员演很多电影，一部电影有很多演员。演员卡上只有一格 FID 只能放一部电影，所以要另开一张"演员–电影配对"表。

Exercise Q3：(a) Actors star in films；(b) SEX 布尔 → {TRUE, FALSE}；(c) ACTOR PK AID、FK FID；FILM PK FID；(d) 只有一个 FID 字段时演员只能连到一部电影，STARRING 每对一行，PK FID+AID。

Exercise Q1：没有唯一字段 → 违反 entity integrity；只准输入数字的表单 = validation，维持 domain integrity。

ex.q: List every film with its actors using FILM, STARRING, ACTOR.
ex.a:
SELECT F.FNAME, A.ANAME
FROM FILM F, STARRING S, ACTOR A
WHERE F.FID = S.FID AND S.AID = A.AID;
(demo)
ex.az: 三表 JOIN。

ex.q: How many films has each actor starred in?
ex.a:
SELECT A.ANAME, COUNT(*) FROM ACTOR A, STARRING S
WHERE A.AID = S.AID GROUP BY A.ANAME;
Each actor: 2. Impossible to store with a single FID field.
ex.az: 每人 2 部；单一 FID 字段做不到。

ex.q: A student fixes the problem by adding FID1, FID2, FID3 to ACTOR. Why is this poor?
ex.a:
1. An actor with 4 films still doesn't fit; most actors leave fields NULL.
2. Searching 'all actors in film 2' needs three conditions.
3. Use the linking table STARRING.
ex.az: FID1/2/3 不够用又浪费；应用 STARRING。

demo.query:
SELECT F.FNAME, A.ANAME, S.ROLE
FROM FILM F, STARRING S, ACTOR A
WHERE F.FID = S.FID AND S.AID = A.AID
ORDER BY F.FID;
demo.note: STARRING holds one row per actor–film pair.

ex.q: Which line keeps entity integrity, which referential, which domain?
ex.a: PRIMARY KEY → entity; REFERENCES → referential; CHECK / data type → domain.
ex.az: PRIMARY KEY 实体；REFERENCES 参照；CHECK 域。

ex.q: Write one CREATE TABLE line using all three.
ex.a: CREATE TABLE STUDENT (SID CHAR(5) PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL, CNO INT CHECK (CNO BETWEEN 1 AND 30), CID INT REFERENCES CLUB(CID));
ex.az: 一行同时用三种。

ex.q: A student writes WHERE CID = NULL and mysqldump ... < f.sql. Fix both.
ex.a:
1. WHERE CID IS NULL.
2. Backup writes out: mysqldump ... > f.sql.
ex.az: 改用 IS NULL；备份用 >。

mc.q: How does a relational database organise data?
o: In a tree of parent and child nodes
In tables of rows and columns
As a list of key–value pairs only
mc.e: A relational database organises data in tabular form; each row is a record.
mc.ez: 关系式数据库用表格（行和列）组织数据。

mc.q: Which type of database was the first to be developed and is now almost replaced by the relational database?
mc.e: The hierarchical database came first and is now obsolete.
mc.ez: 层次式数据库最早出现，现已过时。

mc.q: In a DBMS, an entity type is usually represented by a
mc.e: Entity type → table.

mc.q: In a DBMS, an entity is usually represented by a
mc.e: Entity → record (row / tuple).

mc.q: In a DBMS, a relationship is usually represented by
mc.e: Relationships are implemented by foreign keys between tables.
mc.ez: Relationship 用 foreign key 表示。

mc.q: In a DBMS, the domain of an attribute is implemented by
mc.e: Domain → data type and constraint.
mc.ez: Domain 用数据类型和约束实现。

mc.q: Another name for a record in a table is a
mc.e: A record is sometimes referred to as a tuple.

mc.q: Which of the following is a conceptual object rather than a physical object?
mc.e: Transactions, organisations, courses and jobs are conceptual objects.

mc.q: Which set of entity type and attributes is NOT correct?
mc.e: Weight is an attribute of computers; computers should be the entity type.
mc.ez: Weight 是 computers 的属性。

mc.q: Which set of entity type and attributes is NOT correct?
mc.e: Age is an attribute of patients, not an entity type.
mc.ez: Age 是 patients 的属性。

mc.q: Which of the following is a derived attribute?
mc.e: BMI can be calculated from weight and height.
mc.ez: BMI 可由体重身高计算。

mc.q: A table stores OPEN, CLOSE and BHOUR (business hours) of shops. Which statement is correct?
o: BHOUR must be the primary key
mc.e: BHOUR is the time difference between OPEN and CLOSE.
mc.ez: BHOUR 由 OPEN 和 CLOSE 算出。

mc.q: Why is it usually better to store a person's birthday rather than age?
o: Age cannot be stored as an integer
Birthday does not change, so data need not be updated frequently; age can be calculated
mc.e: Age changes every year; birthday does not.
mc.ez: 年龄每年变，生日不变，年龄可以计算出来。

mc.q: A relationship in a relational database usually represents a
mc.e: Relationships are verbs, e.g. join, manage.

mc.q: Which set of entity types and relationship is correct?
o: Lesson, Teacher: X is taught by Y
Patient, Doctor: X is married to Y
mc.e: A lesson is taught by a teacher. Products are sold by shops; height is an attribute.

mc.q: Which set of entity types and relationship is correct?
o: Payment, Recipient: X is received by Y
Author, Book: X is written by Y
Duration, Concert: X is the time occupied by Y
mc.e: A payment is received by a recipient. Authors write books; duration is an attribute; employees are employed by companies.

mc.q: 'Students study Physics, Chemistry or Biology.' What are the entity types?
mc.e: Specific subjects are entities of the entity type Subject.
mc.ez: Physics 等是 Subject 的实体，不是实体类型。

mc.q: 'Departments are managed by managers.' With X = Department and Y = Manager, the relationship is
mc.e: Passive voice: X is managed by Y.

mc.q: STUDENT.CID references CLUB, which holds CID values 1, 2, 3, 4. A student need not join any club. What is the domain of STUDENT.CID?
mc.e: Values come from CLUB.CID, plus NULL for no club.

mc.q: Which set of attribute and domain is NOT reasonable?
o: Region: one of {'New Territories', 'Kowloon', 'Hong Kong Island'}
mc.e: Exchange rates are real numbers and can be below 1 or above 10.
mc.ez: 汇率应为实数，可小于1或大于10。

mc.q: Which set of attribute and domain is NOT reasonable?
o: Age of a bar customer: an integer at least 18
Job title: a string of 60 characters at most
Day of the week: a date within {'1970-01-01' .. '2099-12-31'}
mc.e: A day of the week is not a date.

mc.q: A student ID is a 6-digit number and some IDs start with 0. The most suitable data type is
mc.e: Leading zeros are lost if stored as an integer.

mc.q: A field stores a phone number such as 3320-2310. The most suitable data type is
mc.e: It contains '-' and no arithmetic is done on it.

mc.q: Which data type is most suitable for a field PAID that records whether a student has paid?
mc.e: Yes/no values → Boolean.

mc.q:
What does the following SQLite query return?
SELECT CAST('007512' AS INTEGER)
mc.e: Casting to integer drops the leading zeros, so 7512.
mc.ez: 转整数后前导零消失，得 7512。

mc.q: Which keyword declares a variable-length string of at most 40 characters?
mc.e: VARCHAR(n) is variable length; CHAR(n) is fixed length.

mc.q: A DATE value occupies about
mc.e: DATE: 3 bytes (Table 4.7).

mc.q: What is a database schema?
o: A backup file of a database
A text string that describes a database table
The index table of a field
A rule that checks domain values
mc.e: Schema: TABLE (FIELD1, FIELD2, ...).
mc.ez: Schema 是描述表的文字串。

mc.q: In a schema such as STUDENT (SID, NAME, CLASS), which key is usually underlined?
mc.e: The primary key is underlined.

mc.q: Which statement about a candidate key is NOT correct?
o: It stores unique data for every record
It may consist of more than one field
mc.e: A candidate key cannot be NULL.

mc.q: NAME in STUDENT currently has no duplicated values. Why is it still not a candidate key?
o: Two students may share the same name
mc.e: Uniqueness must hold for all possible data.

mc.q: Which statement about NULL is correct?
o: NULL has the data type integer
NULL means no data is stored and has no data type
NULL is the same as an empty string in every DBMS
mc.e: NULL is no data; 0 is an integer or real number.

mc.q: Table T has SCORE values 80, 0 and NULL. What does SELECT AVG(SCORE) FROM T return?
mc.e: AVG ignores NULL but counts 0: (80+0)/2 = 40.

mc.q: In STUDENT(SID, NAME, CLASS, CNO, EMAIL), which is a composite key?
mc.e: Removing either CLASS or CNO gives duplicates; the others are not minimal or not unique.
mc.ez: CLASS+CNO 是 minimal 的复合键。

mc.q: Why is SID+EMAIL NOT a composite key?
o: SID alone is already a candidate key, so the key is not minimal
SID and EMAIL have different data types
mc.e: A composite key must be minimal.

mc.q: Which set of entity type and candidate key is correct?
o: Student: Hong Kong identity card number
mc.e: No two students share an HKID number. A not unique; B not minimal; C not unique.

mc.q: How many primary keys can a table have?
o: As many as its foreign keys
mc.e: Many candidate keys, but only one primary key.

mc.q: STUDENT has candidate keys SID, EMAIL and CLASS+CNO. Why is SID the best choice of primary key?
o: It does not change, while email and class number may change
It is the only key with numbers
It is a foreign key in STUDENT
mc.e: Students may change email; CLASS+CNO changes every year.

mc.q: A foreign key in table X is always
o: the primary key of another table Y
mc.e: X is the host table, Y the parent table.

mc.q: STUDENT.CID references CLUB.CID. Which is the parent table?
mc.e: The referenced table (CLUB) is the parent; STUDENT is the host.
mc.ez: 被引用的 CLUB 是 parent table。

mc.q: Which statement about foreign keys is correct?
o: A table can have at most one foreign key
A foreign key value can never be NULL
A table can have more than one foreign key
A foreign key must be unique in the host table
mc.e: e.g. GAME has PID and GID.

mc.q: Club data is stored in CLUB and STUDENT stores only CID. Which is an advantage?
o: Club teacher changes need updating only in CLUB
CID can be NULL in CLUB
mc.e: STUDENT need not be updated when club details change.
mc.ez: 学会资料改了只需改 CLUB。

mc.q: STUDENTCLUB stores student and club details in one table; 3 students are in Science Club. How many records must be updated to change Science Club's teacher?
mc.e: Every Science Club student's record holds the teacher.

mc.q: GAME(ID, NAME, PNAME, GID, WEBSITE, PHONE, PRICE). After moving publisher data to PUBLISHER(ID, NAME, WEBSITE, PHONE), which fields remain in GAME?
mc.e: PNAME, WEBSITE, PHONE describe publishers and are replaced by PID.

mc.q: Instead of changing PRICE during a 2-week sale, a field DISCOUNT is added. What is the main advantage?
o: The original price is kept and can be restored by setting DISCOUNT to 0
PRICE can become a primary key
mc.e: Overwriting PRICE would lose the original price.

mc.q: What does indexing a field create?
o: A copy of the whole table sorted by that field
An index table containing the indexed field and pointers to the related records
mc.e: Only the indexed field plus a pointer is stored.

mc.q: Why can a DBMS use binary search on an indexed field?
o: The index table is sorted by that field
The field is a primary key
mc.e: Binary search needs sorted data.

mc.q: Which is a disadvantage of indexing a field?
o: The index takes storage space and must be updated when data changes
The field can no longer be updated
The field must become the primary key
mc.e: Updating the index takes time; it also takes storage.

mc.q: An index table has 15 sorted entries. In the worst case, how many searches does binary search need?
An index table has 1000 sorted entries. In the worst case, how many searches does binary search need?
15 book titles are in a sorted index. Using binary search with middle = (low+high) div 2, how many searches are needed to find the 14th title?
mc.e: Positions checked: 8, 12, 14.

mc.q: Which fields are most suitable to index?
o: Fields that are updated very often but rarely searched
mc.e: Only frequently searched fields should be indexed.
mc.ez: 只为常搜寻的字段建索引。

mc.q: Entity integrity is concerned with
o: the validity of the foreign key
the existence and validity of the primary key
the data types of the attributes
mc.e: Table 4.17.

mc.q: Referential integrity is concerned with
o: the validity of the foreign key
the primary key not being NULL
mc.e: Table 4.17.

mc.q: Domain integrity is concerned with
o: the data types and constraints of the attributes
mc.e: Table 4.17.
mc.ez: 域完整性关注数据类型和约束。

mc.q: Which situation violates entity integrity?
o: A foreign key value is NULL
The primary key contains a duplicated value
mc.e: Primary key must be unique and not NULL.
mc.ez: 主键重复违反实体完整性。

mc.q:
SID is the primary key of STUDENT and '03493' already exists. What happens to
INSERT INTO STUDENT (SID, NAME) VALUES ('03493', 'Zoe')
mc.e: Duplicate primary key is rejected (UNIQUE constraint failed).

mc.q: Which is NOT stopped by referential integrity on STUDENT.CID → CLUB.CID?
o: Inserting a student with a CID not in CLUB
Deleting a club referenced by students
Inserting a student with CID NULL
Changing a referenced CLUB.CID to a new value
mc.e: NULL foreign keys are allowed.

mc.q: CLUB has CIDs 1 to 4; students reference CIDs 1, 2 and 4 only. With foreign keys enforced, which statement succeeds?
o: UPDATE CLUB SET CID = 9 WHERE CID = 4
mc.e: CID 3 is not referenced, so it can be deleted.

mc.q: A table has CHECK (CNO BETWEEN 1 AND 30). Which value of CNO is accepted?
mc.e: BETWEEN is inclusive.

mc.q: Given CHECK (LENGTH(SID) = 5), which SID is accepted?
mc.e: Exactly 5 characters.

mc.q: A shop record has CLOSE = '20:90'. Which integrity is violated?
mc.e: 20:90 is not a valid time.

mc.q: A table has fields CLASS, CLASSNO, GENDER, SNAME and every field (and CLASS+CLASSNO) contains duplicates. Which integrity is most likely violated?
mc.e: No possible primary key.

mc.q: STUDENT has SROW = 'S' though rows are 1 to 5, and CID 3169 which is not in CLUB; SCLN+SROW can be the primary key. Which integrities are violated?
mc.e: Referential (3169) and domain ('S').
mc.ez: 参照完整性及域完整性。

mc.q: A shop is removed from SHOP, and PRODUCT.SID references SHOP. To keep referential integrity, what should be done?
o: Remove (or reassign) the products sold at that shop
Remove the primary key of SHOP
mc.e: Products referencing the removed shop must go too.

mc.q: An online form allows only numbers to be entered for menu choices. This data control mainly maintains
mc.e: Validation keeps values inside the domain.
mc.ez: 验证输入值属域完整性。

mc.q: In SQLite, which statement must be run so foreign key constraints are enforced?
mc.e: SQLite enforces FKs only when the pragma is on.

mc.q: What is a rollback?
o: Restoring a database to its previous state
mc.e: Definition from 4.4.

mc.q: Why must a database be backed up regularly?
o: So that it can be rolled back if errors corrupt the data
mc.e: Backups make rollback possible.

mc.q:
STUDENT has 3 students in 6A and 7 in 5A. A teacher runs
UPDATE STUDENT SET CLASS = '6A' WHERE CLASS = '5A';
DELETE FROM STUDENT WHERE CLASS = '6A';
How many records remain?
mc.e: All 10 become 6A, then all are deleted.

mc.q: Which command exports database SCHOOL to school.sql?
mc.e: mysqldump exports with >; mysql imports with <.

mc.q: Which command restores school.sql into database SCHOOL?
mc.e: mysql runs a SQL file.
mc.ez: mysql 执行 SQL 文件还原。

mc.q: A file made by mysqldump mainly contains
o: SQL statements such as CREATE TABLE and INSERT INTO
mc.e: They recreate the tables with the same data.
mc.ez: 含 CREATE TABLE 和 INSERT INTO。

mc.q: A program updating 10,000 payments in ACCOUNT stopped halfway at an unknown point. What should the administrator do?
o: Run the program again from the start immediately
Roll back the database to the state before the program ran, then rerun
mc.e: Some payments may be half done; rerunning would double some.
ROLLBACK undoes the delete.

mc.q: If the command prompt says 'mysqldump' is not recognized, what should you check?
o: The PATH environment variable includes the MySQL bin folder
The table has a primary key
mc.e: Lab 4.1 note.
mc.ez: 把 MySQL bin 加到 PATH。

sq.q:
A secondary school teacher created two tables A and B to store data of school events and student participants. Students are aged 11 to 18.
ADescription
EIDUnique identity number of each event
ENAMEName of the event
EDATEDate of the event
FEEParticipation fee in dollars, e.g. 34.5
FINISHEDWhether the event has finished
BDescription
SIDUnique 6-digit identity number of each student; some start with zeros
EIDIdentity number of the event the student participates in
AGEAge of the student
PAIDWhether the student has paid the fee

parts.q: State the entity types of A and B.
parts.ms: School events and students respectively [1]

parts.q: Suggest a data type for EID, EDATE and FEE in A.

FEE: real / float (34.5 has a decimal part) [1]

parts.q: Suggest a data type for SID and PAID in B. Explain your choice for SID.

SID: characters, since it may start with 0 and leading zeros would be lost as an integer [1]
PAID: Boolean [1]

parts.q: What is the domain of AGE?

sq.q:
A manager created tables A and B.
A(PID, PNAME, STOCK, PRICE, SID): products, with SID being the shop that sells them.
B(SID, SNAME, OPEN, CLOSE, BHOUR): shops, with daily opening time, closing time and business hours.

parts.q: State the entity types of A and B.
parts.ms: Products and shops respectively [1]

parts.q: Suggest a data type for PNAME, STOCK and PRICE.
parts.ms:
PNAME: characters; STOCK: integer [1]
PRICE: real / float [1]

parts.q: Which field of B is a derived attribute? Explain briefly.
parts.ms:
BHOUR [1]
It is the time difference between OPEN and CLOSE, so it can be calculated [1]

parts.q: What is the domain of OPEN?
What is the relationship between the entity types of A and B?
parts.ms: B sells A / A is sold by B [1]

sq.q: BOOK(ISBN, BNAME, ANAME, ANAT, AAGE, PDATE, PAGE, PRICE, PID) stores books, including author name, nationality and age. PUBLISHER(PID, PNAME, PHONE, LOCATION) stores publishers.

parts.q: Write the schemas of BOOK and PUBLISHER. Underline the primary keys and state the foreign keys.
parts.ms:
BOOK (ISBN, BNAME, ANAME, ANAT, AAGE, PDATE, PAGE, PRICE, PID), Foreign key: PID [1]
PUBLISHER (PID, PNAME, PHONE, LOCATION), Foreign key: N/A [1]

parts.q: Suggest data types for PDATE, PAGE and PRICE.
parts.ms:
PDATE: date; PAGE: integer [1]
PRICE: real / float [1]

parts.q: A table AUTHOR is created with identity code AID; data relating to authors is removed from BOOK. Write the updated schema of BOOK and the schema of AUTHOR.
parts.ms:
BOOK (ISBN, BNAME, AID, PDATE, PAGE, PRICE, PID), Foreign key: AID, PID [1]
AUTHOR (AID, ANAME, ANAT, AAGE), Foreign key: N/A [1]

parts.q: State one advantage of storing authors' birthdays instead of ages.
parts.ms:
Age changes every year but birthday does not [1]
so the data need not be updated frequently; age can be calculated from the birthday [1]

sq.q: A video game platform uses GAME(ID, NAME, PNAME, GID, WEBSITE, PHONE, PRICE) and GENRE(ID, NAME, RES). PNAME, WEBSITE and PHONE describe the publisher; PHONE is e.g. 3320-2310; PRICE is e.g. 30.9.

parts.q: Write the schemas of GAME and GENRE, underlining primary keys and stating foreign keys.
parts.ms:
GAME (ID, NAME, PNAME, GID, WEBSITE, PHONE, PRICE), Foreign key: GID [1]
GENRE (ID, NAME, RES), Foreign key: N/A [1]

parts.q: Suggest data types for PHONE and PRICE with reasons.
parts.ms:
PHONE: characters, contains '-' and no calculation [1]
PRICE: real / float, e.g. 30.9 [1]

parts.q: A table PUBLISHER with identity code is created. Write the updated GAME schema and the PUBLISHER schema.
parts.ms:
GAME (ID, NAME, PID, GID, PRICE), Foreign key: PID, GID [1]
PUBLISHER (ID, NAME, WEBSITE, PHONE), Foreign key: N/A [1]

parts.q: A two-week discount is given. The administrator adds a field DISCOUNT instead of updating PRICE. State one advantage.
parts.ms:
The original price is not lost [1]
After two weeks, DISCOUNT can simply be set to 0 to restore the original prices [1]

sq.q: STUDENT(SID, NAME, HKID, CLASS, CNO, EMAIL) stores students of ABC Secondary School. SID is a student identity code; EMAIL is a personal email address.

parts.q: List all candidate keys of STUDENT.
parts.ms:
SID, HKID, EMAIL [1]
CLASS + CNO (composite key) [1]

parts.q: Explain why NAME is not a candidate key even if no two current students share a name.
parts.ms: Two students may share the same name in future, so uniqueness is not guaranteed [1]

parts.q: Explain why SID + EMAIL is not a composite key.
parts.ms: It is not minimal: SID alone is already unique, so removing EMAIL gives no duplicates [1]

parts.q: Which candidate key should be the primary key? Give a reason by comparing with EMAIL and CLASS + CNO.
parts.ms:
SID [1]
Email may be changed by the student and CLASS + CNO usually changes every year, while SID does not change [1]

sq.q: Index table on BNAME of 15 books (sorted alphabetically), with binary search using middle = (low + high) div 2.

parts.q: State why an index allows binary search.
parts.ms: The indexed field in the index table is sorted [1]

parts.q: How many searches are needed to find the 8th title and the 14th title?
parts.ms:
8th: 1 search [1]
14th: 3 searches (8, 12, 14) [1]

parts.q: In the worst case, how many searches are needed for 15 titles, and for 1000 titles?
Why should we not index all fields in a table?
parts.ms:
Each index table takes extra storage space [1]
The index must be updated when indexed data changes or records are added, which takes time [1]

sq.q: PRODUCT(PID, PNAME, STOCK, PRICE), SHOP(SNAME, ADDRESS, OPEN, CLOSE, OID), OWNER(OID, ONAME, OPHONE). One SHOP record has OPEN 09:30 and CLOSE 20:90.

parts.q: Based on the data, which type of integrity is violated? Explain briefly.
parts.ms:
Domain integrity [1]
20:90 is not a valid time / outside the domain of CLOSE [1]

parts.q: SHOP has no primary key defined. Which type of integrity does it violate?
parts.ms: Entity integrity [1]

parts.q: Suggest a primary key for SHOP and explain.
parts.ms:
ADDRESS [1]
No two shops share the same full address [1]

parts.q: SHOP's primary key is used as a foreign key in PRODUCT to show where products are sold. To maintain referential integrity, what should be done if a record in SHOP is removed?
parts.ms: The records of all products sold at the removed shop should be removed as well [1]

sq.q: A football contest uses PLAYER(PNAME, TID, TNAME, SNO, POS), TEAM(TID, TNAME, GID, PTS) and GROUP(GID, GNAME). SNO (squad number) is unique within a team.

parts.q: State the primary key and foreign key (or N/A) of each table.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: PLAYER: PK TID + SNO, FK TID [1]
TEAM: PK TID, FK GID [1]
GROUP: PK GID, FK N/A [1]

parts.q: One attribute in PLAYER is redundant. Which one? Explain briefly.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: TNAME [1]
It can be obtained from TEAM using TID, and storing it again may cause inconsistency [1]

parts.q: A team withdraws and the organiser deletes its TEAM record without further action. Which integrity may be violated? How can it be fixed?
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: Referential integrity: PLAYER records still reference the deleted TID [1]
Delete (or update) the related PLAYER records of that team [1]

parts.q: Positions can be Goalkeeper, Defender, Midfielder or Forward. A record has POS 'Attacker'. Which integrity is violated?
parts.ms: Suggested answer: Domain integrity [1]

parts.q: A table POSITION(POS, POSTYPE) maps 0–3 to the four positions and PLAYER.POS becomes an integer foreign key. Give two advantages when PLAYER has over 30000 records.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: Less storage: integers are shorter than repeated strings [1]
Changing a position's name updates one row in POSITION only / invalid or misspelt positions are prevented [1]

sq.q: Steven stores actors and films: ACTOR(AID, ANAME, SEX, AGE, FID) and FILM(FID, FNAME, FYEAR). SEX is Boolean.

parts.q: State the relationship between ACTOR and FILM in one sentence.
parts.ms: Suggested answer: Actors star in films [1]

parts.q: What is the domain of SEX?
parts.ms: Suggested answer: {TRUE, FALSE} / {0, 1} [1]

parts.q: Steven removes FID from ACTOR and creates STARRING(FID, AID, CTYPE, ROLE). Why?
parts.ms: Suggested answer: An actor can star in many films (and a film has many actors); one FID field allows only one film per actor [1]

parts.q: A website lets users search films by name, actors by name, and view films by year. Which fields should be indexed?
parts.ms: Suggested answer: FNAME, ANAME and FYEAR [1]

parts.q: A film was removed from FILM and its STARRING records were also removed. Later the film must be added back but the STARRING data is not remembered. Suggest one action.
parts.ms: Suggested answer: Roll back / restore the database (or those tables) from a backup made before the deletion [1]

sq.src: Textbook EA Ch4 Chapter Exercise Q3 (p.240), based on DSE 2014 2A Q2

sq.q: PAYMENT(TID, PAYERID, PAYEEID, AMOUNT, TTIME) and ACCOUNT(AID, UNAME, DEPOSIT). PAYERID and PAYEEID refer to accounts.

parts.q: Write the schema of PAYMENT, underlining the primary key and stating the foreign keys.
parts.ms:
PAYMENT (TID, PAYERID, PAYEEID, AMOUNT, TTIME) [1]
Foreign key: PAYERID, PAYEEID [1]

parts.q: After a payment is made, how should ACCOUNT be updated?
parts.ms:
The payer's deposit is reduced by the amount [1]
The payee's deposit is increased by the amount [1]

parts.q: A program updating ACCOUNT for 10,000 payments was aborted at an unknown point. What should the administrator do? Explain why.
parts.ms:
Roll back the database to the previous state (before the program ran) and rerun [1]
Some payments may be halfway done, e.g. payer deducted but payee not credited, so data is inconsistent [1]

sq.q: STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS) holds 3 students in 6A and 7 students in 5A. At a new school year a teacher wants to remove 6A students and promote 5A students to 6A.

parts.q: Write the two SQL statements in the correct order.
parts.ms:
DELETE FROM STUDENT WHERE CLASS = '6A' [1]
then UPDATE STUDENT SET CLASS = '6A' WHERE CLASS = '5A' [1]

parts.q: The teacher runs them in the reverse order. Describe the result.
parts.ms:
All 5A students become 6A first [1]
then all 6A students are deleted, leaving the table empty (0 records) [1]

parts.q: Define rollback and state what must be done regularly so a rollback is possible.
parts.ms:
Rollback: restoring a database to its previous state [1]
Back up the database regularly [1]

parts.q: Write the MySQL commands to back up database SCHOOL to school.sql as user root, and to restore it.
parts.ms:
mysqldump -u root -p SCHOOL > school.sql [1]
mysql -u root -p -h localhost SCHOOL < school.sql [1]

sq.q: Ms Chan's tea-party order form stores data in MEALORDER(ENAME, AGE, APPETISER, MAINCOURSE, NEEDCUTLERY). AGE has data type p and NEEDCUTLERY data type q.

parts.q: Mr Lee says MEALORDER violates a type of integrity. State it and explain.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: Entity integrity [1]
There is no primary key / no field is guaranteed unique, e.g. two employees may share a name [1]

parts.q: Fix the problem and write the schema of MEALORDER.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: Add a field OID (order identity code) [1]
MEALORDER (OID, ENAME, AGE, APPETISER, MAINCOURSE, NEEDCUTLERY) [1]

parts.q: Apart from character, suggest reasonable data types for p and q.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: p: integer [1]
q: Boolean [1]

parts.q: The form only allows numbers for appetiser and main course choices. What kind of data control is it, and which integrity does it maintain?
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: Validation (e.g. type / range check) [1]
Domain integrity [1]

parts.q: The menu often changes and every record had to be updated. How could this mass update have been prevented?
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: Store menu items in a separate table (e.g. MENU(MID, MNAME)) [1]
and store only the item code in MEALORDER as a foreign key, so a change updates one record in MENU [1]

pr.task: Tables STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) are loaded. STUDENT.CID is a foreign key referencing CLUB.CID. List each student's NAME together with the NAME of the club they joined (column alias CNAME). Students with no club are not shown.
pr.taskz: 已载入 STUDENT 和 CLUB。STUDENT.CID 是引用 CLUB.CID 的外键。列出每位学生的 NAME 和所参加学会的名称（别名 CNAME），没参加学会的不用显示。
pr.solution: SELECT S.NAME, C.NAME AS CNAME FROM STUDENT S, CLUB C WHERE S.CID = C.CID;

check.expected_sql: SELECT S.NAME, C.NAME AS CNAME FROM STUDENT S, CLUB C WHERE S.CID = C.CID;

pr.task: Using STUDENT and CLUB, show every club's NAME and the number of students in it (alias NUM), including clubs with no members (NUM = 0). This shows why keeping CLUB as a separate table is useful: English Club's data is kept even though no student has joined.
pr.taskz: 用 STUDENT 和 CLUB 显示每个学会的 NAME 及人数（别名 NUM），没有成员的学会也要显示（NUM = 0）。可见独立的 CLUB 表能保留没有成员的学会资料。
pr.solution: SELECT C.NAME, COUNT(S.SID) AS NUM FROM CLUB C LEFT JOIN STUDENT S ON C.CID = S.CID GROUP BY C.CID, C.NAME;

check.expected_sql: SELECT C.NAME, COUNT(S.SID) AS NUM FROM CLUB C LEFT JOIN STUDENT S ON C.CID = S.CID GROUP BY C.CID, C.NAME;

pr.task: PRODUCT(PID, PNAME, PRICE, COST) does not store profit, because profit is a derived attribute. Write a query showing PNAME and PROFIT (= PRICE − COST, rounded to 1 decimal place with ROUND) for every product, ordered by PROFIT from highest to lowest.
pr.taskz: PRODUCT 不储存利润，因为利润是衍生属性。写查询显示每件产品的 PNAME 和 PROFIT（= PRICE − COST，用 ROUND 取 1 位小数），按 PROFIT 由高到低排序。
pr.setup:
CREATE TABLE PRODUCT (PID CHAR(4) PRIMARY KEY, PNAME VARCHAR(30), PRICE FLOAT, COST FLOAT);
INSERT INTO PRODUCT VALUES ('P001','Pencil',5.5,2.0),('P002','Ruler',12.0,7.5),('P003','Eraser',4.0,1.2),('P004','Notebook',18.9,11.0),('P005','Glue',9.0,9.5);
pr.solution: SELECT PNAME, ROUND(PRICE - COST, 1) AS PROFIT FROM PRODUCT ORDER BY PROFIT DESC;

check.expected_sql: SELECT PNAME, ROUND(PRICE - COST, 1) AS PROFIT FROM PRODUCT ORDER BY PROFIT DESC;

pr.task: AUTHOR(AID, ANAME, DOB) stores birthdays instead of ages, because age changes every year. Show ANAME and the author's AGE in whole years on the date 2026-09-01. Hint (SQLite): CAST((julianday('2026-09-01') - julianday(DOB)) / 365.25 AS INTEGER). (In MySQL you would use TIMESTAMPDIFF(YEAR, DOB, '2026-09-01').)
pr.taskz: AUTHOR 储存生日而非年龄。显示 ANAME 及在 2026-09-01 时的整数年龄 AGE。提示（SQLite）：CAST((julianday('2026-09-01') - julianday(DOB)) / 365.25 AS INTEGER)（MySQL 可用 TIMESTAMPDIFF）。
pr.setup:
CREATE TABLE AUTHOR (AID INT PRIMARY KEY, ANAME VARCHAR(40), DOB DATE);
INSERT INTO AUTHOR VALUES (1,'Amy Chan','1980-03-15'),(2,'Tom Ho','1995-11-02'),(3,'Kelly Lam','2001-01-20'),(4,'Peter Wu','1972-09-10');
pr.solution: SELECT ANAME, CAST((julianday('2026-09-01') - julianday(DOB)) / 365.25 AS INTEGER) AS AGE FROM AUTHOR;

check.expected_sql: SELECT ANAME, CAST((julianday('2026-09-01') - julianday(DOB)) / 365.25 AS INTEGER) AS AGE FROM AUTHOR;

pr.t: Why NAME is not a candidate key
pr.tz: 为何 NAME 不是候选键
pr.task: A candidate key must store unique data. Write a query that finds every NAME that appears more than once in STUDENT, with the number of times (alias CNT).
pr.taskz: 候选键必须唯一。写查询找出在 STUDENT 中出现多于一次的 NAME，以及出现次数（别名 CNT）。
pr.setup:
CREATE TABLE STUDENT (SID CHAR(5), NAME VARCHAR(40), CLASS CHAR(2), CNO INT, EMAIL VARCHAR(40));
INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('03493','Ada','3A',1,'ada@abcss.edu.hk'),('03496','Clem','3B',15,'clem@abcss.edu.hk'),('03505','Eva','3B',28,'eva@abcss.edu.hk'),('03506','Gabe','3C',15,'gabe@abcss.edu.hk'),('03510','Finn','3B',7,'finn@abcss.edu.hk'),('03513','Ada','3C',12,'ada2@abcss.edu.hk'),('03517','Ben','3A',9,'ben@abcss.edu.hk');
pr.solution: SELECT NAME, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM STUDENT GROUP BY NAME HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

check.expected_sql: SELECT NAME, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM STUDENT GROUP BY NAME HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

pr.t: CNO alone is not a key
pr.task: CLASS+CNO is a composite key because removing either field gives duplicates. Write a query listing each CNO value shared by more than one student, with the number of students (alias CNT).
pr.taskz: CLASS+CNO 是复合键，因为拿走任何一个字段都会重复。写查询列出被多于一位学生共用的 CNO 及人数（别名 CNT）。
pr.setup:
CREATE TABLE STUDENT (SID CHAR(5), NAME VARCHAR(40), CLASS CHAR(2), CNO INT, EMAIL VARCHAR(40));
INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('03493','Ada','3A',1,'ada@abcss.edu.hk'),('03496','Clem','3B',15,'clem@abcss.edu.hk'),('03505','Eva','3B',28,'eva@abcss.edu.hk'),('03506','Gabe','3C',15,'gabe@abcss.edu.hk'),('03510','Finn','3B',7,'finn@abcss.edu.hk'),('03513','Ada','3C',12,'ada2@abcss.edu.hk'),('03517','Ben','3A',9,'ben@abcss.edu.hk');
pr.solution: SELECT CNO, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM STUDENT GROUP BY CNO HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

check.expected_sql: SELECT CNO, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM STUDENT GROUP BY CNO HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

pr.tz: 找出违反参照完整性的记录
pr.task: Foreign keys were not enforced and some bad data got in. List SID, NAME and CID of students whose CID is not NULL but does not exist in CLUB.
pr.taskz: 外键没有被强制，混入了错误数据。列出 CID 不是 NULL 但在 CLUB 中不存在的学生的 SID、NAME、CID。
pr.solution: SELECT SID, NAME, CID FROM STUDENT WHERE CID IS NOT NULL AND CID NOT IN (SELECT CID FROM CLUB);

check.expected_sql: SELECT SID, NAME, CID FROM STUDENT WHERE CID IS NOT NULL AND CID NOT IN (SELECT CID FROM CLUB);

pr.tz: 找出违反实体完整性的记录
pr.task: SID is meant to be the primary key of this table, but no primary key was defined. List the distinct SID values that appear more than once (alias SID) so they can be fixed. (Then also think: which record breaks entity integrity because its SID is NULL?)
pr.taskz: SID 本应是主键，但没有定义。列出出现多于一次的 SID（不重复列出），以便修正。（再想想：哪条记录因 SID 为 NULL 而违反实体完整性？）
pr.setup:
CREATE TABLE ENROL (SID CHAR(5), NAME VARCHAR(40), SUBJECT VARCHAR(20));
INSERT INTO ENROL VALUES ('03493','Ada','ICT'),('03496','Clem','M2'),('03493','Ada2','Physics'),(NULL,'Gabe','ICT'),('03510','Finn','ICT'),('03510','Finn','Chem'),('03517','Ben','ICT');
pr.solution: SELECT SID FROM ENROL WHERE SID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY SID HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

check.expected_sql: SELECT SID FROM ENROL WHERE SID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY SID HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

pr.tz: 找出违反域完整性的记录
pr.task: Domains: SID is exactly 5 characters; SEX in {'M','F'}; CLASS in {'1A','1B','1C','1D'}; CNO in {1 .. 30}. List the SID and NAME of every record that breaks at least one of these domains.
pr.taskz: Domain：SID 刚好 5 个字符；SEX ∈ {'M','F'}；CLASS ∈ {'1A','1B','1C','1D'}；CNO ∈ {1 .. 30}。列出违反至少一个 domain 的记录的 SID 和 NAME。
pr.setup:
CREATE TABLE STUDENT (SID CHAR(5), NAME VARCHAR(40), SEX CHAR(1), CLASS CHAR(2), CNO INT);
INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('03493','Ada','F','1A',1),('0349','Clem','F','1B',15),('03505','Eva','X','1B',28),('03506','Gabe','M','1E',15),('03510','Finn','M','1B',31),('03513','Dio','M','1C',12),('03517','Ben','M','1A',0);
pr.solution: SELECT SID, NAME FROM STUDENT WHERE LENGTH(SID) <> 5 OR SEX NOT IN ('M','F') OR CLASS NOT IN ('1A','1B','1C','1D') OR CNO NOT BETWEEN 1 AND 30;

check.expected_sql: SELECT SID, NAME FROM STUDENT WHERE LENGTH(SID) <> 5 OR SEX NOT IN ('M','F') OR CLASS NOT IN ('1A','1B','1C','1D') OR CNO NOT BETWEEN 1 AND 30;

pr.tz: 用 DISCOUNT 计算最终价
pr.task: Instead of overwriting PRICE during a sale, GAME has a DISCOUNT field (0.2 = 20% off). Show NAME and FINAL = PRICE × (1 − DISCOUNT), rounded to 2 decimal places, for the games of publisher PID = 7 only.
pr.taskz: 促销时不覆盖 PRICE，而用 DISCOUNT 字段（0.2 = 八折）。只显示出版商 PID = 7 的游戏的 NAME 及 FINAL = PRICE × (1 − DISCOUNT)，取 2 位小数。
pr.setup:
CREATE TABLE GAME (ID INT PRIMARY KEY, NAME VARCHAR(40), PID INT, PRICE FLOAT, DISCOUNT FLOAT);
INSERT INTO GAME VALUES (1,'Sky Racer',7,30.9,0.2),(2,'Pixel Farm',3,45.0,0),(3,'Moon Base',7,60.0,0.5),(4,'Word Duel',5,12.5,0),(5,'Robo Chess',7,25.0,0.1);
pr.solution: SELECT NAME, ROUND(PRICE * (1 - DISCOUNT), 2) AS FINAL FROM GAME WHERE PID = 7;

check.expected_sql: SELECT NAME, ROUND(PRICE * (1 - DISCOUNT), 2) AS FINAL FROM GAME WHERE PID = 7;

pr.tz: 通过 STARRING 处理多对多
pr.task: ACTOR(AID, ANAME), FILM(FID, FNAME, FYEAR) and STARRING(FID, AID, CTYPE, ROLE) are loaded. List FNAME and ANAME for every main character (CTYPE = 'Main character'), ordered by FNAME then ANAME.
pr.taskz: 已载入 ACTOR、FILM、STARRING。列出所有 CTYPE = 'Main character' 的 FNAME 和 ANAME，按 FNAME 再按 ANAME 排序。
pr.solution: SELECT F.FNAME, A.ANAME FROM FILM F, STARRING S, ACTOR A WHERE F.FID = S.FID AND S.AID = A.AID AND S.CTYPE = 'Main character' ORDER BY F.FNAME, A.ANAME;

check.expected_sql: SELECT F.FNAME, A.ANAME FROM FILM F, STARRING S, ACTOR A WHERE F.FID = S.FID AND S.AID = A.AID AND S.CTYPE = 'Main character' ORDER BY F.FNAME, A.ANAME;

pr.t: Promote a class in the right order
pr.task: New school year: remove the 6A students, then promote every 5A student to 6A. Write the two statements in the correct order, then finish with SELECT SID, NAME, CLASS FROM STUDENT ORDER BY SID; (the result of this last SELECT is checked). Try the wrong order too and see the table become empty: that is when a rollback is needed.
pr.taskz: 新学年：先删除 6A 学生，再把 5A 学生升到 6A。按正确次序写出两条语句，最后加上 SELECT SID, NAME, CLASS FROM STUDENT ORDER BY SID;（检查这条 SELECT 的结果）。也试试错误次序，看表变空，这时就需要 rollback。

pr.task: Write CREATE TABLE statements for CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM) and STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, CNO, CID) that enforce: entity integrity (primary keys), referential integrity (STUDENT.CID references CLUB) and domain integrity (SID exactly 5 characters, SEX in M/F, CLASS in 1A–1D, CNO 1 to 30). Then insert one valid club and one valid student. Compare with the model answer.
pr.taskz: 写 CLUB 和 STUDENT 的 CREATE TABLE，要求：实体完整性（主键）、参照完整性（STUDENT.CID 引用 CLUB）、域完整性（SID 5 个字符、SEX 为 M/F、CLASS 为 1A–1D、CNO 1–30）。再插入一个有效学会和一个有效学生，与参考答案比较。

check.model: Model answer: CLUB has CID as PRIMARY KEY. STUDENT has SID CHAR(5) PRIMARY KEY (entity integrity); CHECK constraints LENGTH(SID) = 5, SEX IN ('M','F'), CLASS IN ('1A','1B','1C','1D'), CNO BETWEEN 1 AND 30 (domain integrity); FOREIGN KEY (CID) REFERENCES CLUB(CID) (referential integrity). Insert the club before the student, because the student's CID must already exist in CLUB. In SQLite, run PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON; for the foreign key to be enforced.

pr.t: Split a table and write schemas
pr.task: BOOK(ISBN, BNAME, ANAME, ANAT, AAGE, PDATE, PAGE, PRICE, PID) stores author data inside every book record. Design an improved structure: write the schemas (mark the primary key) and CREATE TABLE statements for BOOK and a new AUTHOR table, storing the author's date of birth instead of age.
pr.taskz: BOOK 每条记录都重复存作者资料。设计改良结构：写出 BOOK 及新 AUTHOR 表的 schema（标明主键）和 CREATE TABLE，作者改存出生日期而非年龄。
pr.solution:
CREATE TABLE AUTHOR (
  AID INT PRIMARY KEY,
  ANAME VARCHAR(40),
  ANAT VARCHAR(30),
  DOB DATE
);
CREATE TABLE BOOK (
  ISBN CHAR(13) PRIMARY KEY,
  BNAME VARCHAR(100),
  AID INT,
  PDATE DATE,
  PAGE INT,
  PRICE FLOAT,
  PID INT,
  FOREIGN KEY (AID) REFERENCES AUTHOR(AID)
);

check.model:
Model answer:
BOOK (ISBN, BNAME, AID, PDATE, PAGE, PRICE, PID), Foreign key: AID, PID
AUTHOR (AID, ANAME, ANAT, DOB), Foreign key: N/A
Key points: author fields move to AUTHOR with a new identity code AID; BOOK keeps only AID as a foreign key; DOB is stored because age is a derived attribute that changes every year; ISBN is characters (may contain leading zeros / hyphens); PRICE is real.

chs.tz: 数据库设计与 ER 图

cards.tz: 好的与坏的数据库设计
cards.en:
Intuition: think of a messy school bag. If every worksheet is thrown in one pocket, you find things slowly and keep extra copies "just in case". A database is the same.

The rule: a good design is

  • organised: each table is about one thing (students, classes, subjects);
  • efficient: each fact is stored once;
  • easy to use: tables are linked in a logical way by keys.

A bad design causes slow performance, data inconsistency (two copies of a fact that disagree) and difficulty in retrieving data.

Two tools in this chapter fix this: the ER diagram (plan before building) and normalisation (remove repeated data).

Exam wording: "A well-designed database is organised, efficient and easy to use. Tables are clear and concise, each table contains only the necessary data, and tables are related in a logical way." "A poor design leads to data redundancy, data inconsistency and difficulty in retrieving data."
cards.zh:
直觉：像一个乱糟糟的书包：所有作业塞一格，找东西慢，还会复印很多份"以防万一"。数据库也一样。

规则：好设计要

  • organised：每个表只讲一件事（学生、班、科目）；
  • efficient：每个事实只存一次；
  • easy to use：表之间用 key 合理连接。

坏设计会导致 slow performance、data inconsistency（同一事实两份副本不一致）、difficulty in retrieving data。

本章两大工具：ER diagram（先规划再建表）和 normalisation（去掉重复数据）。

考试写法："A well-designed database is organised, efficient and easy to use..."；"A poor design leads to data redundancy, data inconsistency and difficulty in retrieving data."

ex.q: A shop keeps one big table SALE(SALEID, CNAME, CADDR, CPHONE, ITEM, PRICE). Every sale repeats the customer's address and phone. Give two problems.
ex.a:
1. The same address is stored in many records → data redundancy, wasting storage.
  2. If the customer moves, every record must be changed. Miss one and the database holds two addresses → data inconsistency.
  3. Better: a CUSTOMER table (each customer once) and SALE keeps only the customer ID as a foreign key.
ex.az:
1. 同一地址存很多次 → 冗余浪费空间。
  2. 客户搬家要改很多条，漏改就不一致。
  3. 改进：拆出 CUSTOMER 表，SALE 只存客户 ID（外键）。

ex.q: A library has tables BOOK(BID, TITLE, AUTHOR) and LOAN(BID, MEMBERID, DUEDATE). Is this a good design? Why?
ex.a:
1. Each table is about one thing: books or loans → organised.
  2. Title is stored once in BOOK; LOAN only stores BID → no repeated titles → efficient.
  3. LOAN.BID links to BOOK.BID → related in a logical way.
  4. So it is a good design.
ex.az:
1. 每表只讲一件事。
  2. 书名只在 BOOK 存一次。
  3. 用 BID 合理连接。所以是好设计。

ex.q: A student says: "Storage is cheap now, so repeating data in a table is not a problem." Is this right?
ex.a:
1. Mistake: only thinking about storage space.
  2. The real danger of repeated data is inconsistency: when one copy is updated and another is not, the database gives two different answers.
  3. Repeated data also causes update, insertion and deletion anomalies (section 5.4).
  4. Right answer: redundancy wastes space and risks inconsistent or lost data.
ex.az:
1. 错误：只考虑空间。
  2. 真正问题是不一致：改了一份没改另一份。
  3. 还会造成三种 anomaly（5.4）。
  4. 正确：冗余既浪费空间，也会导致数据不一致或丢失。

demo.query: SELECT SID, SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH FROM STUDENT WHERE CLASS='3B';
demo.note: Bad design: class 3B's teacher is stored in 4 rows. We changed only one row, so 3B now has two different teachers: inconsistent data.

cards.en:
Intuition: an architect draws a plan before building a house. An ER diagram is the plan of a database, drawn before any table is created.

Key words:

  • Entity type: a kind of thing we store data about (Student, Class).
  • Attribute: a property of the entity (Student name).
  • Relationship: how two entity types are linked (Student belongs to Class).

The rule (ER → tables):

  • each entity type → one table
  • each attribute → one field
  • each relationship → a link by foreign key (or an extra table)

Exam wording: "An ER diagram represents the entity types, attributes and relationships of a relational database. It helps decide the table structures before the tables are created."
cards.zh:
直觉：建筑师盖房前先画图。ER diagram 就是数据库的设计图，在建表之前画。

术语：

  • Entity type（实体类型）：要存数据的一类东西（Student、Class）。
  • Attribute（属性）：实体的特征（Student name）。
  • Relationship（关系）：两类实体怎样连（Student belongs to Class）。

规则：entity type → table；attribute → field；relationship → foreign key（或额外的表）。

考试写法："An ER diagram represents the entity types, attributes and relationships of a relational database. It helps decide the table structures before the tables are created."

ex.q: A SCHOOL ER diagram has entity types Student (Student ID underlined, Student name) and Class (Class name underlined, Room number), joined by 'Belong to'. Write the tables.
ex.a:
1. Two rectangles → two tables: STUDENT and CLASS.
  2. Attributes → fields: STUDENT(SID, SNAME), CLASS(CLASSNAME, ROOMNUM).
  3. Underlined → primary keys: SID and CLASSNAME.
  4. 'Belong to' (many students in one class) → add CLASSNAME to STUDENT as a foreign key: STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CLASSNAME).
ex.az:
1. 两个长方形 → 两个表。
  2. 属性 → 字段。
  3. 下划线 → 主键。
  4. Belong to → STUDENT 加外键 CLASSNAME。

ex.q: Textbook Checkpoint 5.1: rectangles Animal, Zone, Species; Animal has ellipses Animal name (underlined), Weight, Date of birth. (a) List the tables. (b) Attributes and primary key of Animal?
ex.a:
1. One table per rectangle: ANIMAL, ZONE, SPECIES.
  2. Animal's attributes: Animal name, Weight, Date of birth.
  3. The underlined one, Animal name, is the primary key.
ex.az:
1. 每个长方形一个表。
  2. Animal 的属性是三个椭圆。
  3. 下划线的 Animal name 是主键。

ex.q: A student writes: "An ER diagram shows the records stored in each table." Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: an ER diagram shows structure, not data.
  2. It shows entity types, attributes and relationships, i.e. what tables and fields will exist and how they link.
  3. Records (rows such as 'Ada, 3A') never appear in an ER diagram.
ex.az:
1. 错误：ER 图画的是结构，不是数据。
  2. 它只显示实体、属性、关系。
  3. 具体记录不会出现在 ER 图中。

frames.en: Two rectangles: Student and Class. Each will become a table.
frames.zh: 两个长方形 Student、Class，各成一个表。

frames.en: Ellipses: Student ID, Student name; Class name, Room number. Each becomes a field.
The diamond Belong to links them. It becomes a foreign key CLASSNAME in STUDENT.
frames.zh: 菱形 Belong to → STUDENT 中的外键 CLASSNAME。

frames.en:
STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CLASSNAME)
CLASS(CLASSNAME, ROOMNUM)

cards.en:
Intuition: like road signs, each shape has one fixed meaning, so anyone can read the diagram.

ShapeMeansNote
Rectangle ▭Entity typebecomes a table
Diamond ◇Relationshipnamed with a verb: Join, Belong to; may have its own attributes
Ellipse ⬭Attributeunderlined = primary key

Lines join attributes to their entity (or relationship), and entities to diamonds. Colours mean nothing.

How to read: rectangle → diamond → rectangle as a sentence: "Student belongs to Class". From the other side use passive voice: "Zone is managed by Manager".

Exam wording: "Entity types are drawn as rectangles, relationships as diamonds and attributes as ellipses. The primary key attribute is underlined."
cards.zh:
直觉：像交通标志，每个形状意思固定。

形状意思备注
长方形Entity type成为表
菱形Relationship用动词命名；关系也可以有属性
椭圆Attribute下划线 = 主键

线把属性连到实体（或关系），把实体连到菱形。颜色无意义。

读法：长方形→菱形→长方形读成一句话；反方向用被动语态。

考试写法："Entity types are drawn as rectangles, relationships as diamonds and attributes as ellipses. The primary key attribute is underlined."

ex.q: Ellipse 'Treatment date' is connected to the diamond 'Treat' between Doctor and Patient. What does it mean?
ex.a:
1. The ellipse is joined to a diamond, not a rectangle.
  2. So Treatment date is an attribute of the relationship Treat.
  3. Meaning: each time a doctor treats a patient, the date of that treatment is recorded. It belongs to neither doctor nor patient alone.
ex.az:
1. 椭圆连在菱形上。
  2. 所以是关系 Treat 的属性。
  3. 每次某医生治疗某病人的日期。

ex.q: Read the diagram Zone ◇Be managed by◇ Manager as two sentences.
ex.a:
1. Left to right: "A zone is managed by a manager."
  2. Right to left (active voice): "A manager manages a zone."
ex.az:
1. Zone is managed by Manager。
  2. Manager manages Zone。

ex.q: A student draws the entity type Teacher as an ellipse and the attribute Teacher name as a rectangle, and colours keys red. What is wrong?
ex.a:
1. Mistake 1: shapes are swapped. Entity type = rectangle, attribute = ellipse.
  2. Mistake 2: colour has no meaning. The primary key is shown by underlining the attribute.
ex.az:
1. 形状反了：实体是长方形，属性是椭圆。
  2. 颜色没意义，主键要加下划线。

frames.en: Doctor and Patient are rectangles = entity types = tables.
frames.zh: 长方形 = 实体 = 表。

frames.en: Treat is a diamond = relationship: "Doctor treats Patient".
Doctor ID (underlined = PK) on Doctor; Treatment date on the diamond = attribute of the relationship.
frames.zh: 椭圆 = 属性；下划线 = 主键；连在菱形上 = 关系的属性。

cards.t: From ER diagram to table structure and schema
cards.tz: 由 ER 图写出表结构与 schema
cards.en:
Intuition: the ER diagram is the plan; the table structure is the real thing you build in SQL.

Steps:

  1. Each rectangle → a table with a short UPPER-CASE name.
  2. Each ellipse → a field with a short name (Event start time → STARTTIME).
  3. Pick a data type: Character, Integer, Date, Time, Datetime.
  4. Underlined attribute → primary key.
  5. Add foreign keys from the relationships (see 5.3).

A schema is a one-line summary of a table: CLASS(CLASSNAME, ROOMNUM), primary key underlined.

To add a new table to a design: draw a new rectangle with its ellipses, then a diamond linking it to the related entity.

Exam wording: "Each entity type becomes a table and each attribute becomes a field. The underlined attribute is the primary key."
cards.zh:
直觉：ER 图是蓝图，table structure 是用 SQL 真正建出来的东西。

步骤：

  1. 长方形 → 表（大写短名）。
  2. 椭圆 → 字段（短名）。
  3. 选 data type：Character、Integer、Date、Time、Datetime。
  4. 下划线 → 主键。
  5. 按关系加外键（5.3）。

Schema 是表的一行摘要：CLASS(CLASSNAME, ROOMNUM)，主键加下划线。

新增表：画新长方形和椭圆，再用菱形连到相关实体。

考试写法："Each entity type becomes a table and each attribute becomes a field. The underlined attribute is the primary key."

ex.q: Entity Event has attributes Event ID (underlined), Event name, Event start time, Venue. Write the schema and data types.
ex.a:
1. Name the table EVENT; short field names EID, ENAME, STARTTIME, VENUE.
  2. Schema: EVENT(EID, ENAME, STARTTIME, VENUE).
  3. Types: EID Integer, ENAME Character, STARTTIME Datetime, VENUE Character.
  4. See the code block for the CREATE TABLE.
ex.az:
1. 表名 EVENT，字段简称。
  2. 写 schema，主键 EID 下划线。
  3. 选数据类型。

ex.q: A zoo adds Manager (Staff ID underlined, Manager name, Phone, Working hours) to manage zones. How do you add it to the ER diagram?
ex.a:
1. Draw a rectangle Manager.
  2. Draw four ellipses joined to it; underline Staff ID.
  3. Draw a diamond Be managed by between Zone and Manager.
  4. Schema: MANAGER(STAFFID, MNAME, PHONE, WORKHRS).
ex.az:
1. 画长方形 Manager。
  2. 四个椭圆，Staff ID 下划线。
  3. 菱形 Be managed by 连到 Zone。

ex.q: A student writes the schema as EVENT(EID, ENAME, STARTTIME, VENUE) with no underline, and gives STARTTIME the type Character. What is wrong?
ex.a:
1. Mistake 1: the primary key must be underlined in a schema: EVENT(EID, ...).
  2. Mistake 2: a start time stored as Character cannot be sorted or compared correctly (e.g. '9:00' > '10:00' as text). Use Datetime or Time.
ex.az:
1. schema 主键要下划线。
  2. 时间用 Character 无法正确排序比较，应用 Datetime/Time。

notes.t: Create a table called EVENT (from the entity type Event).
notes.tz: 建表 EVENT（来自实体 Event）。

notes.t: EID: integer field; PRIMARY KEY because Event ID is underlined.

notes.tz: ENAME 文本，最多 30 字符。

notes.t: STARTTIME: date and time of the event.

cards.t: Foreign keys are shown by relationships
cards.tz: 外键用关系表示，不画成属性
cards.en:
Intuition: on a map you draw a road between two towns; you don't write the other town's name inside each town. A relationship diamond is the road.

The rule: in an ER diagram, a foreign key is NOT drawn as an ellipse. The link is shown by the relationship. Which table gets the foreign key is decided later, from the cardinality (FK goes on the many side).

Example: LETTER(LID, RADD, PID, MID) with PID → POSTMAN, MID → MAILBOX. Letter only has ellipses Letter ID and Recipient address; diamonds Deliver and Originate from link it to Postman and Mailbox.

Exam wording: "Foreign keys are represented by relationships, not by attributes, in an ER diagram."
cards.zh:
直觉：地图上两城之间画一条路，而不是把对方城名写在城里。菱形就是那条路。

规则：ER 图中外键不画成椭圆，而是用relationship表示。外键放哪个表，建表时按基数决定（放在 many 一方）。

例：LETTER(LID, RADD, PID, MID)，Letter 只画 Letter ID 和 Recipient address 两个椭圆，用菱形 Deliver、Originate from 连 Postman、Mailbox。

考试写法："Foreign keys are represented by relationships, not by attributes, in an ER diagram."

ex.q: PRODUCT(PID, PNAME, PRICE, SID), SID references STORE. A student draws an ellipse 'Store ID' on Product. Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: drawing the foreign key SID as an attribute of Product.
  2. Remove the 'Store ID' ellipse from Product.
  3. Draw a diamond Sell between Store and Product (Store 1 — M Product).
  4. Store Id stays only as Store's own (underlined) key.
ex.az:
1. 错误：把外键画成 Product 的属性。
  2. 删掉该椭圆。
  3. 画菱形 Sell 连 Store 和 Product。

ex.q: LETTER(LID, RADD, PID, MID). Which ellipses does Letter have in the ER diagram?
ex.a:
1. PID and MID are foreign keys → not ellipses.
  2. Letter has only Letter ID (underlined) and Recipient address.
  3. Links: Postman ◇Deliver◇ Letter, Letter ◇Originate from◇ Mailbox.
ex.az:
1. PID、MID 是外键，不画。
  2. 只有 Letter ID 和 Recipient address。

ex.q: Tables BOOK(<u>BID</u>, TITLE, PUBID) and PUBLISHER(<u>PUBID</u>, PNAME). Draw the ER diagram in words.
ex.a:
1. Rectangles: Book, Publisher.
  2. Book ellipses: Book ID, Title. (PUBID is a FK → not drawn on Book.)
  3. Publisher ellipses: Publisher ID, Publisher name.
  4. Diamond Publish: Publisher 1 — M Book (FK is on the many side, BOOK).
ex.az:
1. 两个长方形。
  2. Book 只画 Book ID、Title。
  3. 菱形 Publish，Publisher 1 对 M Book。

demo.title: Turning a foreign key into a relationship

frames.en: LETTER(LID, RADD, PID, MID). PID and MID point to other tables.
Letter keeps only <u>Letter ID</u> and Recipient address as ellipses.
PID → diamond Deliver to Postman; MID → diamond Originate from to Mailbox.

cards.en:
Intuition: must every student join a sports event? Yes → must. May a student skip it? → may. That "must or may" is the participation constraint.

The rule: the participation constraint of a relationship says whether each entity of an entity type takes part in the relationship. Each relationship has two sides; each side is mandatory or optional, shown by a symbol on the line.

Symbol on the line, next to entity BSideMeaning
short bar |Mandatory sideeach A must be linked to at least one B
circle OOptional sideeach A may or may not be linked to a B

Careful (book's way): the symbol is drawn next to the entity being counted. "A student must join a sports event" → the bar | is drawn next to Sports event (Student ◇Join◇ |Sports event). We say "the right side is mandatory".

Exam wording: "The participation constraint specifies whether each entity of an entity type participates in a relationship or not." "Since each student must join a sports event, the right side is mandatory."
cards.zh:
直觉：每个学生都必须参加运动项目吗？必须 → must；可参加可不参加 → may。这就是参与限制。

规则：每个关系有两面（two sides），每面是 mandatory 或 optional，用线上的符号表示。

画在 B 旁边的符号Side意思
短竖线 |Mandatory side每个 A 必须连到至少一个 B
圆圈 OOptional side每个 A 可以有也可以没有 B

注意（课本画法）：符号画在被数的那个实体旁边。“A student must join a sports event” → 竖线画在 Sports event 旁边，称为 “the right side is mandatory”。

考试写法："The participation constraint specifies whether each entity of an entity type participates in a relationship or not." "Since each student must join a sports event, the right side is mandatory."

ex.q: Student ◇Join◇ Sports event. "Every student must join a sports event; some events may have no students." State each side.
ex.a:
1. 'Each student must join an event' counts events per student → symbol next to Sports event → right side mandatory (|).
  2. 'An event may have no students' counts students per event → symbol next to Student → left side optional (O).
ex.az:
1. 每个学生必须参加 → 右面（Sports event 旁）强制 |。
  2. 项目可以没有学生 → 左面（Student 旁）非强制 O。

ex.q: Textbook Example 5.2(a): Computer ◇Be assigned to◇ Student (Computer drawn on the left). 40 computers, 25 students, each student is assigned exactly one computer.
ex.a:
1. 'Each student is assigned one computer' counts computers per student → symbol next to Computer → left side mandatory.
  2. More computers than students, so some computers have no student → symbol next to Student → right side optional.
ex.az:
1. 每个学生必有一台电脑 → Computer 旁（左面）强制。
  2. 电脑多于学生，有些电脑没人用 → Student 旁（右面）非强制。

ex.q: A student draws the bar | next to Student for "each student must join an event".
ex.a:
1. Mistake: putting the symbol next to the entity in the subject of the sentence.
  2. The sentence tells us how many events each student has, so the symbol goes next to Sports event.
  3. Tip: "Each A must/may ... B" → symbol next to B.
ex.az:
1. 错误：把符号画在主语实体旁。
  2. 句子说的是每个学生有几个项目，所以画在 Sports event 旁。
  3. 口诀：“Each A must/may ... B” → 符号画在 B 旁。

frames.en: "Each student must join a sports event." It tells us how many events one student has.
frames.zh: 这句话说的是每个学生有几个项目。

frames.en: Put the mandatory bar | next to Sports event: right side mandatory.
frames.zh: 竖线画在 Sports event 旁：右面强制。

frames.en: "An event may have no students" → circle O next to Student: left side optional.
frames.zh: 圆圈 O 画在 Student 旁：左面非强制。

cards.t: Mandatory and optional sides in real life
cards.tz: 生活中的强制与非强制
cards.en:
Intuition: turn every rule into the pattern "Each A must / may ... B". "must" → mandatory, "may or may not" → optional, and the symbol goes next to B.

Mandatory side examples (from the book):

  • Each employee must belong to one department.
  • Every course must be taught by one or more lecturers.
  • Each vehicle must have a registration plate.

Optional side examples:

  • An employee may or may not have tasks at hand.
  • Each hotel room may or may not be occupied by guests.
  • A citizen may or may not own a vehicle.

Decide from the scenario's words, not your opinion.

Exam wording: "Each employee must belong to one department, so the side next to Department is mandatory."
cards.zh:
直觉：把规则改写成 “Each A must / may ... B”：must → mandatory，may or may not → optional，符号画在 B 旁。

强制例子：每个员工必须属于一个部门；每个课程必须由一位或以上讲师教；每辆车必须有车牌。

非强制例子：员工可以有也可以没有手头任务；酒店房间可能空着；市民可以没有车。

按题目文字判断，不按个人看法。

考试写法："Each employee must belong to one department, so the side next to Department is mandatory."

ex.q: Employee ◇Belong to◇ Department. Each employee must belong to one department; a new department may have no staff yet.
ex.a:
1. 'Each employee must ... department' → bar | next to Department (mandatory).
  2. 'A department may have no staff' → circle O next to Employee (optional).
ex.az:
1. Department 旁强制。
  2. Employee 旁非强制。

ex.q: Citizen ◇Own◇ Vehicle. A citizen may or may not own a vehicle; each vehicle must be owned by a citizen.
ex.a:
1. 'Citizen may or may not own a vehicle' → O next to Vehicle.
  2. 'Each vehicle must be owned by a citizen' → | next to Citizen.
ex.az:
1. Vehicle 旁 O。
  2. Citizen 旁 |。

ex.q: Hotel: Room ◇Be occupied by◇ Guest. A student says "rooms are for guests, so it is mandatory".
ex.a:
1. Mistake: using purpose instead of the rule.
  2. A room may or may not be occupied at a given time → the side next to Guest is optional.
ex.az:
1. 错误：用用途判断。
  2. 房间可以空着 → Guest 旁非强制。

frames.en: "A department may have no staff yet."
"Each department may have no employee." A = Department, B = Employee.
Circle O next to Employee.

cards.en:
Intuition: a school and its principal: every school must have a principal, and every principal must belong to a school.

The rule: both sides mandatory (bar | on both ends). For each entity a there must be at least one related b, and vice versa.

Database effect: no entity on either side can be left unlinked; foreign keys are NOT NULL.

Exam wording: "For each school there must be a principal, and each principal must belong to a school, so both sides are mandatory."
cards.zh:
直觉：学校与校长：每间学校必须有校长，每位校长必须属于一间学校。

规则：两面都强制（两端都是 |）：每个 a 至少有一个 b，反之亦然。

数据库影响：两边都不能落单，外键 NOT NULL。

考试写法："For each school there must be a principal, and each principal must belong to a school, so both sides are mandatory."

ex.q: Textbook Example 5.2(c): Student ◇Belong to◇ Class. Every student belongs to a class; each class has about 20–30 students.
ex.a:
1. Every student belongs to a class → | next to Class.
  2. Each class has 20–30 (≥1) students → | next to Student.
  3. Both mandatory.
ex.az: 1. 两边都强制（每班 20–30 人即至少 1 人）。

ex.q: Order ◇Contain◇ Order line. Every order has at least one line; every line belongs to one order.
ex.a:
1. | next to Order line.
  2. | next to Order.
  3. Case A.
ex.az: 1. 两边都强制 → A。

ex.q: Teacher ◇Be assigned to◇ Class (class teacher). A student says both sides are mandatory.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: each class must have a class teacher, but a teacher may or may not be a class teacher.
  2. So it is case B: | next to Teacher, O next to Class.
ex.az:
1. 错误：老师不一定是班主任。
  2. 应为情况 B。

demo.query: SELECT SCHNAME, PNAME FROM SCHOOL s JOIN PRINCIPAL p ON s.SCHID = p.SCHID;
demo.note: Every school appears with a principal and every principal has a school (SCHID NOT NULL): both sides mandatory.

cards.tz: B. 一边强制一边非强制
cards.en:
Intuition: teachers and classes: each class must have a class teacher, but a teacher may or may not be a class teacher.

The rule: if the side of A is mandatory and that of B is optional:

  • for each b, there must be at least one related a;
  • for each a, there may or may not be a related b.

This is the most common case.

Exam wording: "Each class must have a class teacher, so the side next to Teacher is mandatory; a teacher may or may not be a class teacher, so the side next to Class is optional."
cards.zh:
直觉：每个班必须有班主任，但老师不一定是班主任。

规则：A 面强制、B 面非强制：每个 b 必须有相关 a；每个 a 可有可无 b。最常见。

考试写法："Each class must have a class teacher, so the side next to Teacher is mandatory; a teacher may or may not be a class teacher, so the side next to Class is optional."

ex.q: Member ◇Borrow◇ Loan record. Each loan must be made by a member; a member may have no loans.
ex.a:
1. | next to Member.
  2. O next to Loan.
  3. Case B.
ex.az: 1. Member 旁 |，Loan 旁 O。

ex.q: Textbook Example 5.2(d): Award ◇Be given to◇ Student. 16 subjects × 3 awards = 48 awards, 40 students, ≥5 students per subject.
ex.a:
1. Students are not guaranteed an award → the side next to Award is optional.
  2. Each subject has ≥3 students, so every award has a recipient → the side next to Student is mandatory.
ex.az:
1. 学生不一定得奖 → Award 旁非强制。
  2. 每个奖一定有人得 → Student 旁强制。

ex.q: 48 awards > 40 students, so a student concludes every student must get an award.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: more awards than students does not guarantee each student one; one top student could win many.
  2. Follow the description: students are not guaranteed an award → optional.
ex.az:
1. 错误：奖多于人不代表人人有奖。
  2. 按描述 → 非强制。

demo.query: SELECT t.TNAME, c.CLASSNAME FROM TEACHER t LEFT JOIN CLASS c ON t.TID = c.TID;
demo.note: Every class has a teacher (TID NOT NULL). Ms Ho has no class (NULL): the class side is optional.

cards.en:
Intuition: citizens and diseases: a citizen may or may not have a disease, and a disease may or may not have an infected citizen.

The rule: both sides optional (circle O on both ends). For each a there may or may not be a related b, and vice versa.

Database effect: records on both sides can exist alone; a link table may have no rows for some of them.

Exam wording: "Each citizen may or may not be infected with a disease and each disease may or may not infect a citizen, so both sides are optional."
cards.zh:
直觉：市民与疾病：市民可能没病；某疾病可能没人感染。

规则：两面都非强制（两端都是 O）。

数据库影响：两边记录都可单独存在。

考试写法："Each citizen may or may not be infected with a disease and each disease may or may not infect a citizen, so both sides are optional."

ex.q: Textbook Example 5.2(b): Student ◇Borrow◇ Book.
ex.a:
1. A book is not guaranteed to be borrowed → optional.
  2. Students may choose not to borrow → optional.
  3. Case C.
ex.az: 1. 两边都非强制。

ex.q: Student ◇Join◇ Club. A student may join no club; a new club may have no members.
ex.a:
1. O next to Club.
  2. O next to Student.
ex.az: 1. 两端都 O。

ex.q: A student says optional–optional means the relationship can be deleted from the design.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: optional only means 'not every entity takes part'.
  2. Many students still join clubs, so the links must be stored.
ex.az: 1. 错误：非强制不等于没用。

demo.query: SELECT c.CNAME, COUNT(m.SID) AS MEMBERS FROM CLUB c LEFT JOIN MEMBERSHIP m ON c.CID = m.CID GROUP BY c.CID;
demo.note: Drama has 0 members, and Cat is in no club: both sides optional.

cards.en:
Method:

  1. Find the two entity types and the relationship verb.
  2. Rewrite each rule as "Each A must/may ... B".
  3. Keyword → side type (table below).
  4. Draw the symbol next to B. Write a full sentence as your reason.
KeywordSide
must, every ... at least one, always, exactly onemandatory |
may or may not, not guaranteed, can choose not to, some ... neveroptional O

Hidden clues: "about 20 to 30 students per class" means at least one → mandatory. "More computers than students" means some computers unused → optional.

Exam wording: "Since each [A] must [verb] [B], the side next to [B] is mandatory."
cards.zh:
方法：

  1. 找两个实体和关系动词。
  2. 每条规则改写成 “Each A must/may ... B”。
  3. 按关键词判断。
  4. 符号画在 B 旁，写完整句子作理由。
关键词Side
must / every ... at least one / always / exactly onemandatory |
may or may not / not guaranteed / can choose not tooptional O

隐藏线索：“每班约 20–30 人”= 至少一人 → 强制；“电脑比学生多”= 有电脑没人用 → 非强制。

考试写法："Since each [A] must [verb] [B], the side next to [B] is mandatory."

ex.q: "Each flight must be operated by one aircraft. An aircraft may be under repair and operate no flight." (Flight ◇Be operated by◇ Aircraft)
ex.a:
1. Each flight must ... aircraft → | next to Aircraft.
  2. Each aircraft may ... no flight → O next to Flight.
ex.az:
1. Aircraft 旁 |。
  2. Flight 旁 O。

ex.q: "Each company may own zero or any number of offices. Each office is owned by one company." (textbook)
ex.a:
1. Company may own zero offices → right side (Office) optional.
  2. Each office owned by one company → left side (Company) mandatory.
ex.az:
1. Office 旁非强制。
  2. Company 旁强制。

ex.q: "Each patient must see a doctor." A student marks both sides mandatory.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: this sentence only gives the side next to Doctor (mandatory).
  2. The side next to Patient needs another clue, e.g. "a new doctor may have no patients" → optional. If none is given, state your assumption.
ex.az:
1. 错误：一句话只决定一面。
  2. 另一面要找线索或写假设。

frames.en: "Each company may own zero offices." A=Company, B=Office.
frames.zh: 每间公司可以没有办公室。

frames.en: O next to Office (right side optional).
"Each office is owned by one company" → | next to Company.

cards.en:
Intuition: participation asks "at least one?"; cardinality asks "at most how many?" One or many?

The rule: the cardinality of a relationship specifies how many entities of one entity type can be related to entities of another entity type. It is written as a character beside the line:

Character next to BMeaning
1each A relates to one B at most
M (or N)each A can relate to many B

Like the participation symbol, it is written next to the entity being counted: "A student may join many sports events" → M next to Sports event.

Three types: one-to-one (1:1), one-to-many (1:M), many-to-many (M:N).

Exam wording: "The cardinality specifies how many entities of an entity type can be related to entities of another entity type."
cards.zh:
直觉：参与限制问“至少一个吗？”；cardinality 问“最多几个？”一个还是多个。

规则：基数说明一个实体类型的实体能与另一实体类型的多少个实体相关，用线旁的字符表示：1＝最多一个；M/N＝可以多个。

和参与符号一样，写在被数的实体旁边：“A student may join many sports events” → M 写在 Sports event 旁。

三种：1:1、1:M、M:N。

考试写法："The cardinality specifies how many entities of an entity type can be related to entities of another entity type."

ex.q: "Each department has one department head only; each head leads one department." Cardinality?
ex.a:
1. Each department → 1 head: write 1 next to Head.
  2. Each head → 1 department: write 1 next to Department.
  3. One-to-one.
ex.az: 1. 两边都写 1 → 一对一。

ex.q: "A school has multiple classrooms; each classroom belongs to one school."
ex.a:
1. School → many classrooms: M next to Classroom.
  2. Classroom → one school: 1 next to School.
  3. School 1 — Have — M Classroom: one-to-many.
ex.az: 1. Classroom 旁 M，School 旁 1 → 一对多。

ex.q: "Each student joins one sports event." A student writes 1 next to Student.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: the character goes next to the entity being counted.
  2. The sentence counts events per student → write 1 next to Sports event.
ex.az:
1. 错误：字符写在被数的实体旁。
  2. 应写在 Sports event 旁。

demo.query: SELECT s.NAME, COUNT(e.EID) AS SUBJECTS FROM STUDENT s LEFT JOIN ENROLMENT e ON s.SID = e.SID GROUP BY s.SID;
demo.note: Counting how many electives each student is related to: Clem has 3, so the cardinality next to Elective is 'many'.

cards.tz: 参与限制 vs 基数
cards.en:
Intuition: a lift sign says "minimum 1 person to run, maximum 10 people". Participation = minimum, cardinality = maximum.

Participation constraintCardinality
